prerequisites: Prior knowledge of Electronic and Photonic Devices (2nd semester)
Radiofrequency and Microwave Technologies (7th semester) is advisable.

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to analyze components and their specifications for guided and unguided communication systems.

Ability to select antennas, equipment, and transmission systems, propagation of guided and unguided waves, through electromagnetic, radiofrequency, or optical media, and the corresponding management of radioelectric space and frequency allocation.
Knowledge of basic subjects and technologies, enabling the learning of new methods and technologies, and providing great versatility to adapt to new situations.

Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and aptitudes, understanding the ethical and professional responsibility of the activity of the Telecommunications Technical Engineer.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, evaluations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, task planning, and other similar work in their specific field of telecommunications.

Analyze the propagation of waves through optical media and interpret the influence of attenuation, intermodal and intramodal dispersion, and non-linear phenomena, on the transmission capacity of optical communication links.
Describe optical transmission equipment and systems, establish their parameters, and identify and compare their components based on working frequency bands and transmission capacity.

Describe optical reception equipment and systems, establish their parameters, and identify and compare their components based on working frequency bands, bandwidth, and the presence of noise in the optical communication link.
Explain the operation of optical signal regenerators, identify and characterize their components according to working frequencies and transmission capacity.
Analyze different passive optical components, characterize their behavior, specify their parameters, and identify their use in optical communication systems.
Handle fibers, transmitters, receivers, components and optical measurement equipment, and build and characterize optical communication systems.

syllabus_topics: Propagation of waves guided by optical media.
Types of optical fibers and their manufacturing technology.
Light propagation in fibers: geometric description and electromagnetic description.
Intermodal, intramodal, and mode polarization dispersion in optical fibers.
Attenuation and non-linear phenomena in optical fibers.
Fundamentals of light emission and absorption.
Gain saturation and crosstalk in optical amplifiers.
assessment_rules: In the ordinary call, a minimum score of 4 out of 10 is required for both the theoretical and practical blocks. If these minimums are achieved, the final grade is calculated as (0.7 x Theory) + (0.3 x Practices); otherwise, the grade is the score of the failed part. The extraordinary call involves a theoretical exam and a practical exam, each requiring a minimum of 4 points out of 10. If these minimums are achieved, the final grade is calculated as (0.7 x Theory) + (0.3 x Practices); otherwise, the grade is the score of the failed part. In case of doubt about authorship, a face-to-face defense may be requested.
